markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (96%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class conformal set [F1], but the second model disagrees and only 2 of 5 similar cases are invasive.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 96%, InSitu 4% | Clear lead |
| Conformal set | Invasive only (90% level) | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / OOD percentile 1.0 | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models disagree |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 invasive [F5] | Weak neighbor support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 4, 8, 9) · ↑ invasive · Strongest concept association with invasive carcinoma [F2] · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 9, 10, 11) · ↑ invasive · High score; second-strongest association [F3] · Validated
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (region 3) · context · Below typical; descriptive only [F4] · Weak
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 7) · ↓ invasive · Modest score, negligible weight; InSitu is runner-up · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007), so not shown to reflect the classifier. No Unreliable concept drives this case.

## Could be wrong if
- The second model's differing top class is correct; two of five similar cases are InSitu.
- Image is a simulated, JPEG-degraded frozen section; the suggested margin call [F7] is simulated.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 4, 8, 9**: confirm tumor cells infiltrating stroma, not benign stroma.
2. **Regions 9, 10, 11**: confirm marked pleomorphism in tumor, not reactive change.
3. **Region 7**: look for ducts with confined atypical cells (in situ component).
